subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Risk Aversion for Gains, Risk Seeking for Losses
description: A quick, practical guide to Risk Aversion for Gains, Risk Seeking for Losses.

hook.text: Win $500 for sure, or flip for $1,000? Most take the sure thing. Now reverse it with losses.

buildup.text: Lose $500 for sure, or flip for a chance to lose $1,000 or nothing? Most gamble. Same math, opposite behavior.

discovery.text: People are risk-averse when winning and risk-seeking when losing. The domain flips the preference.

twist.text: This is why people hold losing stocks hoping they'll recover, but sell winning stocks too early.

climax.text: Whether you're in gain or loss territory changes your entire risk appetite. It's automatic, not strategic.

punchline.text: Winning makes you cautious. Losing makes you reckless.

quiz.question: How does domain affect risk preferences?
options: Risk-averse for gains, risk-seeking for losses
